a: A class is a blueprint for creating objects.
An object is an instance of a class with state and behavior.
Encapsulation hides internal state and exposes a controlled interface.
Inheritance lets a class reuse and extend another class.
Polymorphism lets different types respond to the same interface.
Abstraction focuses on essential features and hides details.
A method is a function defined on a class or object.
A constructor initializes a new object.
An interface specifies methods a type must implement.
Composition builds complex types from smaller objects (has-a).
